API contracts and source attribution

Unit 1 · Week 9 · Lesson 1 · Suggested 55-minute plan; adjust to local timing.

Prepare: Official Python open/csv documentation, Python editor, disposable practice folder, week 8 module design and project-workbook.md section 7. Use synthetic data only.

Suggested answers are teacher guidance, not extra assessment tasks. These notes are public.

1. API contracts and source attribution

Suggested time: 2 minutes

Instructional strategy: Learning intention

Success means explain an API beyond web services, identify inputs, outputs, side effects and likely errors from documentation, then record a reused source and the learner’s own contribution. This is the scheduled API/attribution lesson, before two project build workshops later in week 9.

2. Retrieval: module agreements

Suggested time: 5 minutes

Instructional strategy: Individual retrieval and paired explanation

Allow silent recall, then compare with the week 8 design. order_cost takes a valid quantity and returns integer cents. save_order changes persistent storage and needs an agreed failure signal. An unfinished stub deliberately raises NotImplementedError. Use responses to connect student-defined interfaces to library interfaces.

3. An API is a software interface

Suggested time: 6 minutes

Instructional strategy: Worked comparison and classification

API means application programming interface. Programs use documented operations supplied by another component. Python’s open and the csv library are local examples. A web API adds remote communication, but this project needs no account, key or network service. The operation contract describes allowed inputs, results, side effects and errors. Ask learners to classify their own function contract and a library call without assuming all APIs use the internet.

4. Documentation detective

Suggested time: 10 minutes

Instructional strategy: Paired documentation reading and jigsaw explanation

Open the official open and csv.writer documentation linked in the teacher notes. One partner finds file mode, encoding and errors, the other finds writer creation, writerow and newline guidance. Partners explain and complete a four-part contract. Expected: append mode retains existing records, newline="" lets csv control record newlines, encoding="utf-8" makes encoding explicit, writerow receives a row sequence and writes it. Creation of a writer alone does not write a row. open can raise OSError, including PermissionError. Do not copy the entire documentation or memorise every optional parameter. Sources: https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#open and https://docs.python.org/3/library/csv.html#csv.writer

5. A local API in use

Suggested time: 10 minutes

Instructional strategy: Predict, run, investigate and change

Use only a disposable practice folder. This original demonstration appends A01,2,600 as one CSV row. Predict before running, inspect the text file, then change the ID to A02 and quantity/cost to 0 and 0. Both rows should remain. Re-running the unchanged snippet appends a duplicate, so discuss who controls repeated calls. csv writes the record separator, so do not add a separate newline field. The API can quote commas, but the agreed project ID restrictions still apply. The snippet assumes valid values and a writable folder; it is not a complete save_order implementation and has no failure handler. Explain that validation, caller policy and exception handling remain project responsibilities. Sources: official csv and open documentation.

6. A useful source log

Suggested time: 12 minutes

Instructional strategy: Worked example and independent source review

Model a real log entry for this lesson: Source: CS ATAR textbook, Unit 1 Week 9 Lesson 1, site URL and access date. Reused section: original csv practice snippet. Code licence: MIT, retaining the linked copyright/permission notice when distributing reused code. Changes: A01 to A02 and quantity/cost to zero. Own contribution: prediction, run evidence and interface explanation. Then record official Python documentation separately as a consulted reference, with URL, section, access date and what it informed; distinguish consulting documentation from copying its examples. Students audit one actual source from their work and record borrowed section, relevant permission/conditions, changes, own work and permitted assistance in workbook section 7. Follow school rules if used for assessment. If permission is unclear, use an approved source or ask the teacher before reusing. Crediting a source alone does not establish reuse permission.

7. Credit and permission

Suggested time: 5 minutes

Instructional strategy: All-student hinge question and scenario discussion

Correct B. Being publicly visible does not itself establish permission to copy and distribute. Naming the author is attribution, while the licence/permission sets conditions. Avoid a blanket judgement about all classroom copyright exceptions: here the question concerns publishing copied code in the shared textbook/project. Students should use an approved licensed alternative or seek guidance, then record required credit. This is a practical source review, not a new legal or assessment policy.

8. Exit ticket: an interface you can justify

Suggested time: 5 minutes

Instructional strategy: Independent exit ticket

Collect a short contract for csv.writer/ writerow or open: supplied input, result/effect and a relevant failure. Students explain why csv does not enforce the project’s non-negative quantity rule or determine its save-failure policy. Check a completed source entry distinguishes reused material from original work. Next lesson is error classification and debugging; leave full project storage implementation to the scheduled build workshop.
